entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

SDK themes: keep every live theme edit as the phone's draft, not only text

Colour, style and layout edits lived only in the host's blob, which the next
launch or server refresh replaced, and Review & Publish re-applied an older
text draft over them. A designer's colour changes were lost without warning.

- RipulThemeEngine.recordLocalEdit(): every engine mutation (and a host after
  its own theme writes) saves the running theme as the durable draft, once
  per main-thread turn. The draft holds off refreshes and is restored at launch.
- An editor's lease owns the draft; edits made under a host lease (Home cards)
  are kept when it ends.
- Opening Theme Management takes the running theme over the saved draft
  instead of re-applying the older draft.

  are kept when it ends.

  instead of re-applying the older draft.

Call this first when a fix appears not to have worked — it distinguishes 'stale binary' from 'the fix is wrong'. Runs on a remote device. Call device_list_targets to discover devices and their capabilities; pass device to select one.

device.description: Optional. Target a specific connected REMOTE device by its handle (e.g. "iphone-c603") — the value returned as `_device` on a previous result, and the only form guaranteed unique. A display name also works when it matches exactly one device; if it matches several the call fails and lists the handles. If omitted, this chat's working device is used (see device_list_targets); a chat without one uses the only connected device, and several connected devices fail. A device another agent holds refuses the call.

name: reference_bridge_install_cli_for_long_installs
description: "host_bridge_install times out at 30s; a WAC Beta install over the bridge takes ~4 min, so run the ripul-bridge CLI detached"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference

  modified: 2026-10-06T09:45:47.001Z

On 2026-10-06, `scripts/install-wac-device.sh` built WAC Beta, then `devicectl` failed with CoreDeviceError **4016** ("not able to fulfill the requested usage assertion requirements"). The phone was still reachable over the Tailscale bridge.

- The `host_bridge_install` MCP tool gives up after **30 s** ("Native tool timed out after 30000ms"). The WAC install took **233 s**.
- Use the CLI, detached, and poll its log. It waits for the phone's lock (for example an `identify apps` run) by itself:
  `nohup bash -c 'ripul-native-app/device-bridge/ripul-bridge install 17 "/tmp/wac-dd-beta/Build/Products/Release(Beta)-iphoneos/WAC.app" --launch --timeout 300; echo EXIT_CODE=$?' > /tmp/x.log 2>&1 & disown`
- The CLI reads back the build number it installed (`"build": "2026…"`, `"route": "bridge"`). That readback is the proof of delivery.
- Before installing on a shared branch (WAC `v3`), `git fetch` and rebase first. Other agents push Beta builds to `v3` all the time. An app built from a stale tree would put back the phone's older code and drop their fixes.

See [[project_wac_build_verify_and_records_edge_swipe]].

---
name: project_theme_edits_durable_draft
description: Every live theme edit (colour/style/Home cards/tips, not just text) is now saved as the phone's durable theme draft — SDK 0.7.167/0.7.168, WAC Beta 202610061315 (2026-10-06)
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Incident (2026-10-06):** Eden (eden@wac.rocks, temporarily made a Ripul admin so he could publish `wac-v1`) published text changes, but his colour changes were lost. Colour/style edits lived only in WAC's UserDefaults blob `wacThemeOverrideJSON`, which launch, any server refresh, and his own publish all erase (`Theme.swift` remote apply callback removes it). Only text edits went into the SDK's durable draft (`RipulThemeDraft`, Application Support/Ripul/ThemeDrafts). Opening Theme Management re-applied that older text draft over the live colours, so Review & Publish never saw them. The server keeps no theme history, so the colours were unrecoverable.

**Fix:** SDK `RipulThemeEngine.recordLocalEdit()` (called from every engine mutation via `commit()`, and by WAC `ThemeProvider.apply`) saves the running theme over the saved draft through `RipulRemoteThemeClient.recordLocalEdit/saveLocalEdit`. A draft holds off refreshes and is restored at launch. Editor leases own the draft; edits made under a host lease (Home card editor) are saved when the lease ends. `ThemeManagementModel.start` now captures the running theme over the draft instead of re-applying it. `savedDraft` is public (0.7.168); WAC `theme_server local_diff` and the status field `unpublishedDraft` read it.

**Gotchas:** `theme_server local_diff` used to read the blob and said "no edits" after a relaunch. A phone with a draft does NOT receive other people's publishes until it publishes or resets ("Reload server version" / discard_local). The pre-existing test `testNotModifiedRestoresServerOverLocalPreview` fails since 3b89e5524 (a 304 no longer re-applies); this is not a regression from this fix.

Related: [[project_backend_hosted_app_themes]], [[project_cms_delegated_design]] (the model for letting site members publish themes without full admin, which is still not built).

name: project_wac_ota_deploy_flow
description: "WAC iOS OTA install-page + dev/prod IPA deploy — NOW scripted/committed in the WAC repo (scripts/deploy-wac-ota.sh + ota/install.html + docs/ota-deploy.md), backed by R2 bucket wac-ota on the osintsupport Cloudflare account"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d573bbc2-36d1-47c0-90e9-8df774a710a1

The public WAC test-build install page `https://wac-ota.osintsupport.workers.dev/install.html` and its dev/prod IPA distribution **was** an uncommitted /tmp+R2 pipeline (only in past Claude sessions). As of 2026-06-12 it is **committed in the WAC repo** (`WAC_ios_final`): `scripts/deploy-wac-ota.sh` (build→package→manifest→upload + `upload-page`), `ota/install.html` (curated page = source of truth), `docs/ota-deploy.md` (full ref), linked from the WAC root `CLAUDE.md`. Usage: `B=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M); WAC_BUILD_NUMBER=$B scripts/deploy-wac-ota.sh build dev "notes"` (then prod), edit `ota/install.html`, `scripts/deploy-wac-ota.sh upload-page`.

Flavour → scheme → archive config: **dev** = `WAC(Dev)`/`Release(Dev)` (`:3000` backend, isTestingBuild=true → Debug screens visible); **staging** = `WAC(Staging)`/`Release(Staging)` (prod backend, testing build); **prod** = `WAC`/`Release` (prod backend, AppleAppID 1483618032 → isTestingBuild=FALSE → Debug screens HIDDEN).

**CONFIG GOTCHA (broke login once):** the WAC scheme's plain **`Debug` config maps to Dev.xcconfig** (DEV backend `app.workandcommunications.co.uk:3000`, dev app-id 6740474528) — NOT prod. Only **`Release` → Production.xcconfig** (prod `api3...`). So a `-configuration Debug` build points the app at the dev server → login OTP never arrives. Always build prod with `-configuration Release`. (Verify any build's real backend: `plutil -extract BASE raw <App>/Info.plist`.) Fast direct-to-device installs: `scripts/install-wac-device.sh [udid]` (Release, `build` not archive, persistent /tmp/wac-device-dd → incremental ~1-3 min). Device UDIDs: 17 Pro Max 00008150-001C544E0EBA401C, 16 Pro Max 00008140-00080C6E3A52801C. First deploy via this flow: dev+prod build 202606121431 (v2.6.1, auto-pause location + Location debug screen), both live + verified 200.

**Architecture:** `install.html` (hand-maintained, lists builds newest-first) → each build links `itms-services://?action=download-manifest&url=.../manifest-<B>.plist` → manifest points to `.../WAC-<B>.ipa` (bundle id `com.WAC`, bundle-version `<B>`). A small worker `wac-ota.osintsupport.workers.dev` serves these from R2 bucket `wac-ota`. The worker's own source is NOT on disk — appears to be a one-off R2-proxy living only on Cloudflare.

**Build number `B`** = timestamp `YYYYMMDDHHMM` (e.g. `202606110359`). Prod builds locked to MARKETING_VERSION = App Store version (e.g. v2.6.0) so there's no upgrade gate. Prod named `WAC-prod-<B>.ipa` / `manifest-prod-<B>.plist`; dev named `WAC-<B>.ipa` / `manifest-<B>.plist` (dev differs only by backend). All dev-SIGNED (Apple Development, team `C7AA358R56`) → device must be in the provisioning profile + user must trust the developer.

**Build:** `xcodebuild archive -workspace WAC.xcworkspace -scheme WAC -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -archivePath /tmp/WAC-prod-$B.xcarchive CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=C7AA358R56 CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION=$B`.

**GOTCHA 1 — Xcode 26.2 `-exportArchive` is BROKEN** for this app ("Unknown Distribution Error"; `exportOptionsPlist error for key "method" ... found development` — it can't enumerate distribution methods for the watch-container app). Workaround: package the IPA MANUALLY from the archive's already-(dev-)signed `.app` — copy `/tmp/WAC-prod-$B.xcarchive/Products/Applications/WAC.app` into `Payload/`, zip → `WAC-prod-$B.ipa`; verify `unzip -l` shows PK.

**GOTCHA 2 — wrangler multi-account.** `wrangler` sees 3 accounts (Peter@coolrivers.co `acbc570bb776fd33a46c0ba67f9cbbcc`, Peter.maude@ripul.io, a "Ripul" one) → non-interactive uploads FAIL with "Available accounts are…". Fix: the wac-ota bucket is on account `48994301be053cfc75d066dfaed15e35` — pin it. Also `cd /tmp` first so wrangler doesn't write config into a repo dir.

**Upload (R2):**
```
cd /tmp
export CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=48994301be053cfc75d066dfaed15e35   # CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN already set in env
npx wrangler r2 object put "wac-ota/WAC-prod-$B.ipa"      --file /tmp/WAC-prod-$B.ipa      --content-type application/octet-stream --remote
npx wrangler r2 object put "wac-ota/manifest-prod-$B.plist" --file /tmp/manifest-prod-$B.plist --content-type application/xml --remote
npx wrangler r2 object put  wac-ota/install.html         --file /tmp/install.html        --content-type "text/html; charset=utf-8" --remote
```
Verify: `curl -s https://wac-ota.osintsupport.workers.dev/install.html` and `...&cb=$(date +%s)` on the manifest.

**RISK:** ephemeral `/tmp` staging + hand-edited install.html + no committed script = no source of truth; a tmp wipe loses the page/manifests (IPAs survive in R2). Worth committing a real `deploy-wac-ota.sh` + checked-in install.html template into the WAC repo.

**install.html churn is deploy artifact, not foreign WIP (confirmed by Peter 2026-07-14):** `scripts/ship-wac.sh` mutates the in-tree `ota/install.html` on every OTA deploy (its `ota_page` step prepends the new build entry, keeps newest 20) and uploads it to R2. So a dirty `ota/install.html` at session start just means someone shipped OTA — don't treat it as another agent's WIP; commit it (chore) so the tree matches the live page.
- [wac ota deploy flow](project_wac_ota_deploy_flow.md) — WAC iOS OTA install-page + dev/prod IPA deploy — NOW scripted/committed in the WAC repo (scripts/deploy-wac-ota.sh + ota/install.html + docs/ota-deploy.md), backed by R2 bucket wac-ota on the osintsupport Cloudflare account
- [WAC delivery when the phone is away](reference_wac_delivery_when_phone_is_away.md) — CoreDevice 4016 → ripul-bridge CLI install; OTA works without the Cloudflare token; /tmp build cache loses files after 3 idle days

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# WAC "just ship it" — THE default build+deliver entry point. Encodes the standing
# targeting policy so it is NOT re-decided (or re-discovered, with its footguns) each time:
#
#   1. If Peter's iPhone 17 Pro Max is reachable  -> fast incremental build + install + relaunch.
#   2. Otherwise                                   -> fast incremental PROD + BETA OTA builds
#                                                     in parallel, both published on completion.
#   3. No prompts. It picks, in that order, and runs it.
#
# Both paths are FAST incremental (warm /tmp/wac-device-dd, `build` not `archive`, no opt),
# Release config (-> prod backend), and go through -workspace (never a hand-rolled xcodebuild
# against the .xcodeproj — that omits CocoaPods and fails on Alamofire in RotaCardWidget).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/ship-wac.sh                       # auto: device if reachable, else prod+beta OTA
#   scripts/ship-wac.sh <udid>                # auto, but target this device when reachable
#   WAC_TARGET=device scripts/ship-wac.sh     # force device install + relaunch (fails if unreachable)
#   WAC_TARGET=ota    scripts/ship-wac.sh     # force prod+beta OTA regardless
#   WAC_NOTES="what changed" scripts/ship-wac.sh   # OTA release notes (ignored on device path)
#
# STILL LAUNCH DETACHED for the multi-minute build (the session can be recycled mid-build):
#   nohup bash scripts/ship-wac.sh > /tmp/wac-ship.log 2>&1 &
# "Reachable" = the exact UDID shows up as an ELIGIBLE (arch-reporting) iOS destination.
# A disconnected / ineligible device is either omitted or listed without arch -> falls to OTA.
# Run prod + beta OTA builds in parallel; wait for both; exit non-zero if either fails.

content.text:
No, that isn't built. Everything since has been the fix for lost colour edits. Publishing still needs full Ripul admin, which is why Eden still has it.

**Where it stands:**
- The publish route, `PUT /admin/app-themes/:id`, requires `admin:manage_site_keys`, so only global admins pass.
- A theme isn't linked to any site; `app_themes` holds just an id, the document and who last published. So the server can't tell whether `wac-v1` is WAC's to edit.
- The WAC app publishes with the Ripul console sign-in, not the person's WAC login.

**What I'd build, reusing what portals already do for delegated design:**
1. **Link each theme to a site.** Add the site key to `app_themes`, and assign `wac-v1` to WAC's site. A theme with no site stays admin-only, so nothing opens up by accident.
2. **A publish route for site members.** It accepts a publish when the person is an active member of that theme's site and has one of its design roles (the same `designRoles` that already decide who can design the business.wac.rocks portal). Global admins still pass.
3. **Version history and Restore.** This matters more once people other than admins publish, because a publish reaches every phone on its next launch. Today, each publish replaces the last with nothing kept.
4. **The app side.** The SDK publishes to the new route, and a refusal explains which role is needed instead of "no permission". That needs an SDK release and a WAC build.

**Decisions for you:**
- **Which login do designers use?**
  - **Ripul account (simplest):** Eden keeps signing in to the Ripul console, and you add eden@wac.rocks as a WAC site member with a design role.
  - **WAC login:** Eden publishes as his WAC self, matched by email the way business.wac.rocks designers already are. It's better for real customers, who never need a Ripul account, but the WAC app has to send its own sign-in token.
- **Which roles?** Reuse the portal's `designRoles` (one list), or keep a separate list just for the app theme?
- **Publish straight away, or with approval?** Straight away plus history and Restore is what I'd recommend. Approval is safer, but it keeps you as the bottleneck.

Once that's live, Eden's admin can be removed for good. Tell me your choices and I'll build it.

Both Ripul/Alice **202609221721** published through ship-ios.sh with verified OTA manifests and downloaded IPA hashes; phone unreachable, so availability is verified but installation is not. Install each app through Settings > Advanced > Builds. All three native runtime manifests match 14 changed source hashes (`cf0d62a60bff806a57c7fea160fc1fa72e2978d5d527c5437057d90eb82ff57d`); the older web diagnostic stamp alone did not indicate stale runtime code. Full evidence and setup guidance are in the plan. No production team/host assignment was changed for testing.

+**Private by default since 2026-10-06** (Peter asked for it that day; commits `ce02be3b3`, `d2ae9d3f1`, `e36532883`; migration `0061_department_chat_visibility.sql` applied). A chat on a shared Mac belongs to whoever started it and is private until they share it; host-discovered chats belong to the registering account, which still sees everything on its own Mac. Only the creator can share or unshare. `chatVisibleTo` replaced `chatBelongsToMachine` on member commands and the transcript route. The machine room is one room for all members, so `payloadForMember` (in `departmentCommands.ts`) trims lists, sends an answer only to whoever asked and drops other people's chat traffic, live and in history. One chat has several ids, so rows share a `group_id` and the group is what is shared. Share from a chat's long-press menu (native sessions list, web session card). Not a secret: same macOS user, so files on disk stay readable. Known gaps are listed in section 9 of the plan.

The publisher (`toolImages.ts`) writes a `cli_tool_video_<toolUseId>` card. Only https links into `/v1/files/artifacts/` on Ripul's hosts are played.
+- The stills beside a video (`frames: [{ atSeconds, jpegBase64 }]`) are for the model and are not shown as images.
+- The store takes `video/mp4` only as a raw body with a Content-Length and `retention=conversation` (64 MB), and `GET /v1/files/:key` answers byte ranges, which iOS needs to play video.
+- Mac host tools: `record_screen` (start/stop, or `seconds`) and `present_video` (a file on the Mac). They upload with the machine token.
+**Why:** Peter wants video evidence of a testing run, not single screenshots.

+- **A locked Mac records blank.** Behind the lock screen apps stop painting: Safari and the host's own browser tabs recorded as a toolbar over a white page (the document reports `visibilityState: hidden`), and a display recording never returned. The tool now refuses while locked. Check `ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` before blaming the recorder.

+- To judge a recording, use a page that shows a running clock (`/tmp/ripul-video-demo/index.html` was the test): stills taken 3.3 s apart showed the timer 3.3 s apart. A scrolled article proves nothing, as Peter pointed out.

+- `ScreenRecording.swift` and `HostVideoFile.swift` import only system frameworks, so `swiftc` builds them into a command-line harness that inherits the host's Screen Recording permission. It needs `_ = NSApplication.shared` first, or CoreGraphics asserts (`CGS_REQUIRE_INIT`).

name: project_wac_ripul_strangler_auth
description: WAC↔Ripul strangler-fig + BYOA auth — how the SDK/CMS integrates into WAC where WAC owns auth
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 49c136d1-956b-4d96-88d9-e0131cc070ec

Integrating the Ripul native CMS renderer into the **WAC iOS app** where **WAC owns auth**, riding the CMS strangler-fig proxy that is replacing WAC's Rails backend.

**State of the world (already built, discovered 2026-07-05):**
- RipulAgent SDK is **already a WAC dependency** (SPM `ripul-ios-sdk` v0.2.16; agent panel `WACAgentCoordinator` behind `RipulConfig.isAgentEnabled`, off by default).
- Strangler front-door is **live & app-selectable**: `ConfigurationHelper.cmsBaseUrl = "https://llm-proxy.ripul.io/v1/app/"` (catch-all → WAC).
- WAC already runs CMS-native queries but **site-key auth only** (no per-user identity): `JobPrefill.swift` → `POST /v1/cms-definitions/{id}/queries/{slug}/run` + `X-Site-Key` (`pk_live_qhzxe5zpbk2xb1v1lxb4z4sd`, origin `wac-ios.app`).
- **The WAC auth-provider + origin + routes are seeded/tested** in `chrome-extension/packages/payslip/scripts/cms-config.ts` targeting the live WAC CMS `cms_x5xpger1lv3j`. Enrich pipeline seeded DISABLED (ship-dark pattern). Verify which routes are actually enabled.

**WAC auth reality (why standard BYOA doesn't fit):**
- Token is **opaque BCrypt-hashed** in `authentication_tokens` (`secret` + `secret-id` custom headers, NOT Bearer, NOT a JWT). No JWKS → Rails must be the validation authority. Stored in iOS **UserDefaults** (not Keychain), non-refreshable, cleared on logout.
- Identity anchor = **phone/user-id**; **email deliberately never verified** (OTP plan). So Ripul's verified-email RLS join ([[project_byoa_rls_proxy_sso]], [[project_cms_directory_membership]]) is UNSAFE here.

**The design already keys correctly** — `auth_wac` provider: `credentialHeaders:['secret','secret-id']`, introspects `GET <wac>/api/v1/user`, `principalPath:'user.id'` → `principal.forcedUserId` → `bodyCtx.principalId` → RLS `WHERE user_id=@principalId` (handlers.ts:1657). RLS key = **WAC integer user.id, never email**. Cached 45s. Same WAC credential does double duty: proves identity to Ripul (introspection) AND passes through the proxy to Rails. Strangler switch = per-route `bind: proxy→WAC | query→native-SQL`, exact-match beats `/*` passthrough, additive per-table cutover, no app release. `withPrincipalHeader` injects `x-principal-id` downstream.

**The one real gap:** native `CmsClient` only speaks `Authorization: Bearer` (Clerk/site-key) and calls the DIRECT run endpoint (not an app-route), so it never triggers `auth_wac`. Close it via **Option A** (expose queries as `/v1/app/...` routes + `authProviderId:auth_wac`; teach CmsClient a credential mode sending secret/secret-id; load definition via site-key embedded-config not /admin) — MVP, reuses built machinery — or **Option B** (new Ripul endpoint mints short-lived session JWT `sub="wac:<user.id>"` from the WAC creds; renderer uses Bearer; Keychain-storable; clean end-state).

**SHIPPED 2026-07-14 (worker a4da7ad70 + admin UI 47ba79b53, deployed, migration 0036 applied):** opaque portalAuth + invite-only + blocked flag + @principalId binding + admin UI (block toggle, add-by-external-id, opaque settings) are LIVE. Gotcha fixed en route: no-Bearer-token requests 401'd BEFORE the BYOA fallbacks — opaque auth now hooks the missing-token gate in index.ts. NATIVE SHIPPED 2026-07-14: SDK v0.2.20 (monorepo cea42ac01, published via release-public.sh) — CmsClientConfig.portalCredentialProvider (opaque headers INSTEAD of Bearer), fetchPortalMembership, CmsPageLoader member mode + .noAccess state, CmsPage.requiredRoles + CmsPageVisibility (exact mirror of web pageVisibility.ts). WAC 77725db07 (feature/shift-rate-templates): RipulConfig.cmsId+portalCredentials() (preference.secret/secret_id), Testing-hub row "Ripul portal (member mode)" → DebugRipulPortalView. Validate from demo.ripul.io origin WORKS for the WAC key (embedded cms config present, 10 pages). CONFIG LIVE 2026-07-15: WAC key sk_3b7wtby33l2n ALREADY had live Clerk BYOA (clerk.wac.rocks) → shipped **portalAuthOpaque second slot** (81de26490; browser IdP + app creds coexist; opaque gate reads dedicated slot first; UI = switch section not third radio). D1-seeded: portalAuthOpaque {secret/secret-id → origin_wac /api/v1/user, user.id, subPrefix wac} + membershipPolicy invite-only (safe: no directoryTable, zero prior members). First member: wac:465097 (Peter, admin, email join peter.maude@gmail.com). Verified fail-closed: bogus/absent creds → 401; validate still returns clerk. Positive path tests from the WAC app (Testing hub → "Ripul portal (member mode)", needs OTA build installed).

**DECIDED 2026-07-14 (validated plan committed: `chrome-extension/docs/plans/wac-byoa-auth-integration.md`, d7b05d98d):** portal-*membership* path = new `portalAuth.provider:'opaque'` (id-first: `principalIdPath` required, sub=`wac:<user.id>`, email/display metadata only) + **invite-only `membershipPolicy`** (register/me fail closed — today register AUTO-ENROLLS any authed visitor and me JIT-binds from directoryTable, so delete ≠ block) + **`status:'blocked'` column on site_key_owners** (only revocation lever; WAC tokens never expire; 45s cache covers credential validation only, member lookup is live). Also: portal query runs DON'T bind `@principalId` today (only /v1/app/* does) — must bind raw WAC id when opaque-authed. Exactly 4 BYOA fallback points in packages/api/src/index.ts (register/run/design/me, ~1363/1384/1404/1416).

**GOTCHA hit 2026-07-15 — worker regression via parallel main deploy:** the BYOA work lived on ios-sdk/token-inspector; another session's deploy:all from main WIPED the opaque worker → app showed no-access despite perfect config (diagnosed by tailing llm-proxy with bogus creds: no [opaquePortalAuth] logs = old worker). RESOLVED: branch merged to main (2f3691d70) and main is THE working branch now. Second finding: WAC's edge (api3.workandcommunications.co.uk, Cloudflare WAF) 403s bot-like forwarded validation calls — CURL ALWAYS BLOCKED (don't debug with curl!), but the app's real forwarded headers PASS. **E2E PROVEN 2026-07-15: [opaquePortalAuth] authenticated wac:465097 (member: true) — WAC app renders the CMS portal as an invited member, no second login; block toggle verified live.** Diagnostics quieted to matched portal requests only.

**Validated Rails facts (2026-07-14):** `users.email` default `""` + `email_required?=false` + NON-unique → email join unusable (and a priv-esc vector, unverified); phone unique but nullable (social users). **Single-session tokens**: `create_token`→`destroy_old_tokens` destroys ALL tokens AND nils `fcm_id` (user.rb:896-926) → any portal phone+OTP login would log out the iOS app + kill push; browser phase blocked on WAC concurrent-token change. Headers: `secret` + `secret-id` (hyphen); `secret_id` only as param. In-app embedding (SDK passes existing token) sidesteps all of it — zero Rails changes.

**Safety musts:** `/api/v1/user` is the trust boundary (must be real Rails); RLS key=user.id never email; minimize WAC-secret blast radius (prefer B + Keychain); bound 45s revocation lag on logout; fail-closed (401 not silent 0-rows); gate renderer to iOS16+ (app floor is 13 — [[feedback_ios_deploy_device_first]]); writes keep WAC authoritative until cut over; ramp behind a flag.

Related: [[project_cms_transparent_proxy]], [[project_cms_native_renderer]], [[project_api_auth_scope_principal]], [[project_sitekey_mode_vs_token]], [[project_self_hosted_dev_loop_vision]].

**SIDEBAR MERGE 2026-07-15 (SDK v0.2.25, WAC OTA WAC-prod-202607151740):** CMS portal promoted out of debug hub into the REAL slide-out sidebar (RecordMenu, left-edge drawer — NOT the Profile hub). Protocol: SDK `CmsPortalMenuResolver.resolve(cmsId:siteKey:clientConfig:) -> CmsPortalMenu{isMember,role,canDesign,items[]}` contributes role-filtered nav (extracted from shell page's sidebarNav block, filtered via CmsPageVisibility like web filterTree), host renders. WAC: RipulPortalSidebar (cache+refresh+didUpdate), RipulPortalSidebarSection (native "Workplace" section, SF-symbol rows), inserted into RecordMenu scroll content below Status box (re-pins content bottom); gated on isMember; RecordMenuDelegate.didTapPortalPage → RecordsVC_MVVM opens CmsPageView at slug. GOTCHA: new Swift file must be registered in WAC.xcodeproj (checked-in pbxproj, NOT xcodegen) — added on disk only → "cannot find X in scope" compile fail; add PBXBuildFile+PBXFileReference+group+Sources entries (mirror RipulConfig.swift ids).
name: project_byoa_rls_proxy_sso
description: "BYOA Clerk is intended as proxy-SSO (customer auth, Ripul owns user props); RLS ownerField breaks on sub mismatch"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ded5859d-e03a-47e9-b9e3-863db0a6dbf9

CMS Row-Level Security `ownerField` policies read values from a `site_key_owners` row keyed on `(site_key_id, user_id)`, where `user_id` is the Clerk JWT `sub`. For BYOA (bring-your-own-auth) customers, their Clerk tenant mints a **different sub** than the one stored (which came from Ripul's Clerk via admin-add/self-register), so the owner lookup misses → strict-mode RLS denies all rows (`DENY-ALL 1=0`).

**Intended model:** BYOA = proxy SSO. The customer's Clerk only asserts identity; Ripul owns the user props (owner row + customProperties). The fix direction discussed: make the join key **email** and **JIT-bind the sub on first login** — keep first-party (`authSource='ripul'`) keyed on sub. `fetchClerkUserByEmail` uses Ripul's secret key so it can't query the customer's Clerk — email must come from the token.

**UPDATE 2026-06-19 — verified-email extraction is DONE (memory above was stale on this).** `ClerkJwtPayload.email` exists (`types.ts:67-82`); BYOA tokens are cryptographically verified against `portalAuth.jwksUrl` via `verifyClerkJwt(token,env,jwksUrl)` (`auth/clerk.ts:69-141`); `authContext.email = user.email` is set at `index.ts:406` and used by `getSiteKeyOwnerByEmail` in `/v1/site-key/me`, `/register`, and `hydrateRlsContext`. Only dependency: customer's Clerk JWT template must include the email claim. So the remaining TODO is JUST the JIT-bind + directory sourcing, not the claim plumbing. Designed: see [[project_cms_directory_membership]] (plan doc `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/cmsDirectoryMembership.md`) — directory CMS table is the editable user record, `site_key_owners` becomes a JIT-materialised root-of-trust cache, RLS attrs source from the directory's real typed columns.

**Shipped so far (2026-05-29):**
- `[RLS]` diagnostic line (server console + browser console via `rlsDiag` in run responses) — multi-line: auth/site/owner/policy/net. See `summarizeRls` in `cmsDefinitions/handlers.ts`. Distinguishes unauthenticated vs no-owner-row vs ad-hoc-path.
- Break-glass admin relink: `updateSiteKeyOwnerUserId` (storage) + PATCH `owners/:userId` `{newUserId}` + `relinkSiteKeyOwner` service + Relink button in SiteKeyOwnersTab props dialog. Re-points a row's sub, preserving role/props.

**Still TODO:** the real auto-provisioning (email-keyed / JIT sub-bind) so admins don't hand-relink each BYOA user. Ad-hoc editor "Test query" never builds ownerContext (always skips ownerField, lenient); "Test mutation" applies no RLS at all — neither reflects production. Relates to [[project_context_providers]].

name: project_byoa_rls_proxy_sso
description: "BYOA Clerk is intended as proxy-SSO (customer auth, Ripul owns user props); RLS ownerField breaks on sub mismatch"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ded5859d-e03a-47e9-b9e3-863db0a6dbf9

CMS Row-Level Security `ownerField` policies read values from a `site_key_owners` row keyed on `(site_key_id, user_id)`, where `user_id` is the Clerk JWT `sub`. For BYOA (bring-your-own-auth) customers, their Clerk tenant mints a **different sub** than the one stored (which came from Ripul's Clerk via admin-add/self-register), so the owner lookup misses → strict-mode RLS denies all rows (`DENY-ALL 1=0`).

**Intended model:** BYOA = proxy SSO. The customer's Clerk only asserts identity; Ripul owns the user props (owner row + customProperties). The fix direction discussed: make the join key **email** and **JIT-bind the sub on first login** — keep first-party (`authSource='ripul'`) keyed on sub. `fetchClerkUserByEmail` uses Ripul's secret key so it can't query the customer's Clerk — email must come from the token.

**UPDATE 2026-06-19 — verified-email extraction is DONE (memory above was stale on this).** `ClerkJwtPayload.email` exists (`types.ts:67-82`); BYOA tokens are cryptographically verified against `portalAuth.jwksUrl` via `verifyClerkJwt(token,env,jwksUrl)` (`auth/clerk.ts:69-141`); `authContext.email = user.email` is set at `index.ts:406` and used by `getSiteKeyOwnerByEmail` in `/v1/site-key/me`, `/register`, and `hydrateRlsContext`. Only dependency: customer's Clerk JWT template must include the email claim. So the remaining TODO is JUST the JIT-bind + directory sourcing, not the claim plumbing. Designed: see [[project_cms_directory_membership]] (plan doc `chrome-extension/docs/architecture/cmsDirectoryMembership.md`) — directory CMS table is the editable user record, `site_key_owners` becomes a JIT-materialised root-of-trust cache, RLS attrs source from the directory's real typed columns.

**Shipped so far (2026-05-29):**
- `[RLS]` diagnostic line (server console + browser console via `rlsDiag` in run responses) — multi-line: auth/site/owner/policy/net. See `summarizeRls` in `cmsDefinitions/handlers.ts`. Distinguishes unauthenticated vs no-owner-row vs ad-hoc-path.
- Break-glass admin relink: `updateSiteKeyOwnerUserId` (storage) + PATCH `owners/:userId` `{newUserId}` + `relinkSiteKeyOwner` service + Relink button in SiteKeyOwnersTab props dialog. Re-points a row's sub, preserving role/props.

**Still TODO:** the real auto-provisioning (email-keyed / JIT sub-bind) so admins don't hand-relink each BYOA user. Ad-hoc editor "Test query" never builds ownerContext (always skips ownerField, lenient); "Test mutation" applies no RLS at all — neither reflects production. Relates to [[project_context_providers]].

# Claude

## Project Overview

This is a **web application** that provides AI-powered workflow automation and visualization capabilities.

### Architecture

| Component | Status | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| **Web Application** | Active | Primary codebase - React-based workflow platform |
| **Lightweight Extension** | Active | Minimal Chrome extension that augments the web app with browser-specific features |
| **Full Extension** | Legacy | Deprecated full Chrome extension - not actively maintained |

### Development Focus
- **DO**: Develop features in the web application
- **DO**: Keep the lightweight extension minimal (only browser API features)
- **DON'T**: Add new features to the legacy full extension
- **DON'T**: Frame this project as "a Chrome extension" - it's a web application

### Documentation

| Document | Contents |
|----------|----------|
| **[PROJECT-STRUCTURE.md](./docs/PROJECT-STRUCTURE.md)** | Cross-repo guide: chrome-extension, ripul-native-app, ripul-ios-sdk — structure, build commands, message protocol, and cross-repo dependencies |
| **[GLOSSARY.md](./GLOSSARY.md)** | Core domain terms (Tool, Prompt, PromptTool, MCP, etc.) |
| **[EXTENSION-ARCHITECTURE.md](./EXTENSION-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | Extension history, capabilities, and communication protocol |
| **[NATIVE-BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md](./docs/NATIVE-BRIDGE-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | Native iOS ↔ web communication: JS callables (preferred) vs message protocol (legacy) |
| **[DOM-MINIMIZATION-ARCHITECTURE.md](./docs/DOM-MINIMIZATION-ARCHITECTURE.md)** | DOM reduction pipeline, n-tagging strategy, and the semantic-minimization ↔ rehydration bridge |
| **[Tools System Architecture](./docs/architecture/toolsSystemArchitecture.md)** | End-to-end guide: tool definitions → interceptor chain → handler resolution → CLI bridge → native tools. Links to all subsystem docs |
| **[MCP Tool Surfaces](./docs/architecture/mcpToolSurfaces.md)** | Cross-package map of every MCP/tool surface — why each runtime context and surface exists, consumers, transports, name prefixes, and which gates are security vs curation. Start here for anything spanning CLI/native/device/extension tools |
| **[paneLatching.md](./docs/architecture/paneLatching.md)** | Three-pass plan for latching a mirror to an app's own UI element instead of a fixed crop — what each toolkit actually exposes, and why the manifest comes last |
| **[multiViewerMirroring.md](./docs/architecture/multiViewerMirroring.md)** | Multi-viewer window mirroring (implemented 2026-08-27): per-window captures with subscriber sets, one controller driving with loud refusal for the rest, shared crop, controller-only direct transport — plus the plan it grew from and the accepted gaps |
| **[webMcpAutoToolCreation.md](./docs/architecture/webMcpAutoToolCreation.md)** | How agent page interactions automatically become reusable WebMCP tools |
| **[databaseArchitecture.md](./docs/architecture/databaseArchitecture.md)** | D1 database layer: D1Store base class, scoping model, migrations, shared types, and data access patterns |
| **[rbacArchitecture.md](./docs/architecture/rbacArchitecture.md)** | RBAC enforcement: AuthContext flow, access guard policies, team authorization, handler categories |
| **[themingGuide.md](./docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md)** | Theme system: how to use MUI tokens, `alpha()`, `useThemeColors()`, and anti-patterns to avoid |
| **[iOS Styling Guide](../ripul-native-app/docs/ios-styling-guide.md)** | Native iOS glass effects: prefer `.clear` over `.regular`, vibrancy, and glass modifier library |

---

## Code Quality Rules

### After Code Changes
1. **Always run TypeScript compilation check** after making any code changes:
   ```bash
   npx tsgo --noEmit
   ```
2. Fix any TypeScript errors before considering the task complete
3. If there are build errors, investigate and resolve them immediately

### Testing
- Run relevant test commands if they exist
- Verify changes don't break existing functionality

---

## Technical Guidelines

### React Components
- Ensure proper TypeScript types for all components
- Check that all imports are correctly specified
- Verify that component props match their interfaces

### Workflow System
- The workflow graph uses React Flow for visualization
- Panels can appear in both chat log and workflow graph
- Messages with `.toolStatus` suffix appear in the workflow graph
- Base method names (without `.toolStatus`) create UI panels

### Styling
- Use Material-UI (MUI) components and styling system where possible
- Override styles with `!important` when necessary to override inline styles
- Consider both light and dark themes when making UI changes
- **Use MUI theme tokens** (`'text.primary'`, `'action.hover'`, `'divider'`) instead of hardcoded rgba values
- **Never pass string tokens to `alpha()`** — resolve via `theme.palette.X.main` first
- **Use `useThemeColors()` hook** for common color calculations instead of manual `alpha()` calls
- See [themingGuide.md](./docs/features/ui/themingGuide.md) for full details and anti-patterns

### Settings Panels
- For settings dialogs with toggles that reveal more options, follow the established patterns
- See [docs/features/ui/settingsPanelPatterns.md](docs/features/ui/settingsPanelPatterns.md)

### UI Element Traceability
- Add `data-ui` attribute to every rendered element in React components
- Format: `ComponentName.section.element` (e.g., `LLMRequestPanel.header.message`)
- Use static values only - never include runtime data (tool names, IDs, status values, etc.)
- Purpose: Enable tracing from DOM back to source code that created it
- Duplicates are acceptable when the same component is reused
- **MUI compound components** (`TextField`, `Autocomplete`, `Slider`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, etc.) render multiple DOM layers — `data-ui` on the component prop lands on the outer wrapper `div`, not the interactive `<input>`. For any MUI component wrapping a focusable element, also pass `data-ui` through `slotProps`:
  ```tsx
  // ❌ data-ui only reaches the wrapper div
  <TextField data-ui="Foo.bar" />

  // ✅ data-ui also reaches the <input>
  <TextField
    data-ui="Foo.bar"
    slotProps={{ htmlInput: { 'data-ui': 'Foo.bar' } }}
  />
  ```

---

## Deployment & Cloudflare Pages

### CRITICAL: `_routes.json`
- **Location:** `chrome-extension/_routes.json` (copied to `public/` during build)
- **Purpose:** Tells Cloudflare Pages which routes go through Functions vs static files
- `"include"` = routes handled by the Pages Function (`functions/api/[[path]].ts`)
- Everything NOT included is served as static files from `public/`
- **DO NOT** add broad patterns like `"include": ["/*"]` — this routes JS chunks through Functions, which returns `index.html` instead of JavaScript, breaking the entire app
- Current correct config: `/api/*`, the two `/.well-known/` app-link files, `/dl/*` (unlisted downloads from R2, `functions/dl/[[path]].ts`) and `/mac` with `/mac/*` (the address for installing the Mac apps, `functions/mac.ts` and `functions/mac/[product].ts`) — each a narrow path with its own Function

### Chunk Naming & CDN Caching
- Production builds use `chunk-BUILDVERSION-HASH.js` naming (set in `scripts/build.mjs`)
- The build version ensures every deploy produces unique URLs, preventing CDN cache poisoning
- **DO NOT** remove the build version from `chunkNames` — without it, chunks with unchanged content get the same hash across builds, and a single CDN cache poisoning incident becomes permanent
- The `_headers` file sets `/js/*` to `max-age=31536000, immutable` — if the CDN ever caches a wrong response for a chunk URL, it's stuck for a year unless the URL changes

### Incident Reference (2026-03-29)
Missing `_routes.json` in deploys caused Cloudflare to serve `index.html` for JS chunk requests. The immutable cache header then locked the wrong response into the CDN. Fixed by deploying `_routes.json` and adding build version to chunk names.

---

## Development Workflow

1. Understand the requirement
2. Investigate the codebase
3. Make the necessary changes
4. **Run `npx tsgo --noEmit` to check for TypeScript errors**
5. Fix any build errors
6. Test the functionality if possible
7. Document the changes made

---

## Common Commands

```bash
# Check TypeScript compilation
npx tsgo --noEmit

# Build the project
npm run build

# Run tests (if available)
npm test
```

---

## File Structure

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `/src/logging/reactflow/` | Workflow graph components |
| `/src/logging/panels/` | UI panel providers |
| `/src/LLM/Tools/` | Tool handlers for AI interactions |
| `/public/solutions/` | Configuration files for workflows |

---

## Important Patterns

### Dual Message System
Some tools send two messages:
1. **With `.toolStatus` suffix** - for workflow tracking
2. **Without suffix** - for UI panel display

This allows tool authors to control where panels appear.

### Panel Providers
- React-based providers extend `BaseLogPanelProviderReact`
- Providers must implement `canHandle()` and `createLogPanel()`
- Panels can check for methods with or without `.toolStatus` suffix

### API Client & Authentication

**IMPORTANT**: All authenticated API calls must flow through the standard hooks and providers. Never create `ApiClient` instances directly with custom auth.

#### Approved Patterns

**In React components** - Use the hooks:
```typescript
// For LLM Proxy endpoints
const client = useLlmProxyClient();
if (client) {
  await client.get('/v1/endpoint');
}

// For services
const service = useLlmProxyService();
if (service) {
  await service.fetchQuota();
}
```

**Outside React** (only when token is already obtained):
```typescript
// Token already obtained and passed as parameter - OK
const authProvider = new StaticTokenAuthProvider(token);
const client = new ApiClient({ baseUrl, authProvider });
```

#### FORBIDDEN Patterns

**Never** create `ApiClient` with `ClerkAuthProvider` or dynamic token fetching outside the approved hooks:
```typescript
// ❌ WRONG - creates race conditions with token availability
const client = new ApiClient({
  baseUrl: LLM_PROXY_URL,
  authProvider: new ClerkAuthProvider(() => authStore.getToken()),
});
```

#### Why This Matters

Clerk's `getToken()` can temporarily return `null` during session establishment, even when `isSignedIn` is `true`. The approved hooks include retry logic to handle this race condition. Creating custom `ApiClient` instances bypasses this protection and causes auth errors.

#### Existing Approved Locations
- `useLlmProxyClient()` in `src/api/hooks/useApiClient.ts` - React hook with token validation
- `dataProviderAccess.ts` - Uses `ClerkAuthProvider` with retry logic
- Service hooks that depend on `useLlmProxyClient()`

Built 2026-10-06 (monorepo d972fabdd server, SDK 0.7.169, WAC 95ad7f8b0, OTA 202610061555).

- **Server:** `app_themes.site_key_id` (migration 0062) and `app_theme_versions` (every publish, newest 100). `PUT /v1/app-themes/:id` plus `GET /v1/app-themes/:id/versions[/:id]` are authorized by `appThemePublishDenial` in `appThemes/handlers.ts`. Global admin passes. Otherwise the caller must be an active `site_key_owners` member of the theme's site key with a role in that site's CMS `designRoles`. Members match on userId, then on a VERIFIED email; opaque WAC logins carry no email, so only `wac:<id>`. Creating a theme and unlinked themes stay admin-only. Admin `PUT /admin/app-themes/:id?siteKeyId=` links a theme to a site. Auth fallbacks: opaque (`tryOpaquePortalAuth` derives the site key from the theme row) and portal JWKS.

A 403 shows the server's reason. Theme Management has a History section; Restore puts that version into the draft, then Review & Publish.

11	**Incident (2026-10-06):** Eden (eden@wac.rocks, temporarily made a Ripul admin so he could publish `wac-v1`) published text changes, but his colour changes were lost. Colour/style edits lived only in WAC's UserDefaults blob `wacThemeOverrideJSON`, which launch, any server refresh, and his own publish all erase (`Theme.swift` remote apply callback removes it). Only text edits went into the SDK's durable draft (`RipulThemeDraft`, Application Support/Ripul/ThemeDrafts). Opening Theme Management re-applied that older text draft over the live colours, so Review & Publish never saw them. The server keeps no theme history, so the colours were unrecoverable.
12	
13	**Fix:** SDK `RipulThemeEngine.recordLocalEdit()` (called from every engine mutation via `commit()`, and by WAC `ThemeProvider.apply`) saves the running theme over the saved draft through `RipulRemoteThemeClient.recordLocalEdit/saveLocalEdit`. A draft holds off refreshes and is restored at launch. Editor leases own the draft; edits made under a host lease (Home card editor) are saved when the lease ends. `ThemeManagementModel.start` now captures the running theme over the draft instead of re-applying it. `savedDraft` is public (0.7.168); WAC `theme_server local_diff` and the status field `unpublishedDraft` read it.
14	
15	**Gotchas:** `theme_server local_diff` used to read the blob and said "no edits" after a relaunch. A phone with a draft does NOT receive other people's publishes until it publishes or resets ("Reload server version" / discard_local). The pre-existing test `testNotModifiedRestoresServerOverLocalPreview` fails since 3b89e5524 (a 304 no longer re-applies); this is not a regression from this fix.
16	
17	Related: [[project_backend_hosted_app_themes]], [[project_app_theme_site_publishing]] (site designers now publish without admin; 0.7.169 reverted the 0.7.167 Theme Management start() change).
